## Plan

The issue is a loop-carried RAW dependence on `u` between iterations: iteration i writes `u[ju[i]]`, and iteration j>i may read `u[ku[j]]` when `ju[i] == ku[j]`. This couples iterations and blocks parallelization.

**Solution:** Split the single loop into two sequential loops:
1. First loop: all iterations write to `u` (via indirect index `ju[i]`)
2. Second loop: all iterations read from the updated `u` (via indirect index `ku[i]`)

This moves the dependence (writing loop completes before reading loop starts) rather than deleting it. Each loop independently has no inter-iteration dependences: the first loop writes to disjoint `u[ju[i]]` elements, and the second loop writes to disjoint `v[jv[i]]` elements. DiscoPoP should detect both as Do-All loops.

No bounds or initial values need to be re-derived—the loop range remains `i = 1` to `LEN_1D-1`.
